open_points.subject: one-home rule during migration
open_points.text: “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values” conflicts with R0-81: “Production Registry starts without waiting for the other services” and “the copies that remain”
open_points.question: When does the one-home rule become an actual product invariant, and what guarantees apply while other services and legacy instances still keep copies?
options: The invariant applies immediately and production must wait
R0-81 defines an explicit transition period with enumerated temporary copies
The rule is only a future target with no Registry-enforced start condition
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-81 as an explicit transition that overrides the present-tense product statement until every named service change is complete.

open_points.subject: consumer snapshot display name
open_points.text: “A consumer's kept snapshot holds identity — id, display name, status, `customer_ref` — never a personal value” conflicts with R0-68, where Registry omits the display name because it may name a person and cannot be inspected reliably
open_points.question: May a consumer persist a project display name even when it contains a person's name, or must persistent snapshots omit or constrain it?
options: Display name is always permitted identity data
Display name must be omitted from every persisted consumer snapshot
Display names must satisfy an enforceable non-personal naming rule
open_points.default_guess: Omit display names from persisted snapshots unless an enforceable non-personal form is defined.

open_points.subject: object identifying characteristics
open_points.text: The one-home promise names “a customer's personal data” and R0-80 names “the object's address,” while Actors also classifies the object's “identifying characteristics” as `personal_data`
open_points.question: Does the one-home/no-copy rule cover every identifying characteristic of an object, or only its address?
options: Address and all identifying characteristics are Registry-only
Only the address is Registry-only
Each characteristic receives an explicit persistence rule
open_points.default_guess: Apply the one-home rule to every object field classified as `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: authentication bootstrap
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” conflicts with the owner's need to obtain and submit the sign-in form before an authenticated session exists
open_points.question: Which owner-interface requests, if any, may answer before authentication, and what may those answers contain?
options: The sign-in GET and credential-submission POST are explicit unauthenticated exceptions
Authentication is performed by an external gateway before Registry sees any request
The owner session is provisioned out of band and Registry has no unauthenticated sign-in route
open_points.default_guess: Allow only the sign-in form and credential submission unauthenticated, returning no protected data.

open_points.subject: read-project customer projection
open_points.text: “the project card ... with its object and rooms” is one output shared by the owner and personal-data-cleared services, while R0-29 says the owner card has “customer ... included” and R0-80 says contact data reaches the owner alone
open_points.question: Exactly which customer fields does `read a project` return to the owner and to each trusted service?
options: Services receive only `customer_ref`; the owner view separately joins the Customer record
The operation has distinct owner and service projections
Every personal-data-cleared service receives the nested Customer record
open_points.default_guess: Return only `customer_ref` to services and join the full Customer record only in the owner interface.

open_points.subject: customer erasure after fiscal-data addition
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” says “name, phone, e-mail and language are gone” and also says the Customer “keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased,” but the record now also contains tax id and legal name
open_points.question: Does customer erasure remove tax id, legal name, kind, restriction and relationship-end state, or do any of them survive?
options: Erase every living personal and status value, leaving only identity and erased state
Erase contact fields but retain fiscal fields
Provide separate contact-data and fiscal-data erasure actions
open_points.default_guess: Remove all living personal fields, including tax id and legal name, and retain only identity plus erased state.

open_points.subject: billing read with absent fiscal data
open_points.text: Customer creation accepts fiscal data only “when given,” but `read a customer's billing data` promises “tax id and legal name” and defines no outcome when either is absent
open_points.question: What does the billing-data read return when the customer exists but lacks a tax id, legal name or required person name?
options: Return nullable or omitted fields
Refuse as incomplete billing data
Require fiscal data for every customer at creation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with a distinct incomplete-billing-data outcome so a document is not issued with silently missing identity data.

open_points.subject: person name disclosed as billing data
open_points.text: The billing read returns “for a person, the full name as on the document,” while R0-06 defines the name as contact data and R0-80 says “contact data still reaches the owner alone”
open_points.question: Is a person's document name billing data that PresuPro may receive, or contact data that no service may receive?
options: Reclassify the document name as permitted billing data
Keep every person name owner-only and have the owner supply it outside Registry
Allow only company legal names to services
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate document-name billing field that PresuPro may read, rather than silently reclassifying the general contact name.

open_points.subject: restriction scope over fiscal data
open_points.text: R0-59 says “A restriction ... covers the customer's contact data,” but the billing-data action refuses an “erased or restricted customer,” thereby also stopping fiscal-data use
open_points.question: Does restriction block fiscal/billing-data reads as well as contact-data processing?
options: Restriction blocks all customer personal data, including billing data
Restriction blocks contact data only, so billing reads remain allowed
Contact and fiscal restrictions are separate states
open_points.default_guess: Block all customer personal-data disclosures to services while restricted.

open_points.subject: revision preconditions on non-correction mutations
open_points.text: Archive, customer erasure, restriction changes, relationship-end changes and archived-project erasure omit an expected revision and stale-revision failure, although R0-35 says “A change states the revision it was made against”
open_points.question: Which of these mutations must carry the current project or customer revision, and what happens on a stale revision?
options: Every project/customer mutation requires its current revision
Only correction actions require revisions
Destructive actions require revisions, while status toggles do not
open_points.default_guess: Require the current revision for every project or customer mutation and refuse stale requests without change.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: `read the session's access` returns “the access version,” but no text says what the version represents or which actions change it
open_points.question: Which state transitions increment the access version, and can callers use it as a concurrency precondition?
options: Increment for every grant, revoke, active-project change and pending-request change
Increment only when the granted project set changes
Use it as an opaque cache version with separately defined mutation preconditions
open_points.default_guess: Increment it for every change to granted projects, active project or pending request, and accept it as the expected version on owner mutations.

open_points.subject: answering a replaced access request
open_points.text: A newer free-text request “replac[es] the session's earlier pending one,” while `answer an access request` identifies only a session and says merely that “a request no longer pending” is refused
open_points.question: How is an owner's answer bound to the exact pending request they viewed so that a replacement cannot be answered accidentally?
options: Each pending request has an identity supplied when answering
Answering requires the access/request version
The owner always answers whichever request is current, even if it changed after display
open_points.default_guess: Require the pending request identity or access version shown to the owner and refuse a stale answer.

open_points.subject: migration project selection
open_points.text: R0-79 says “the owner picks any of its projects” and then records the owner's choice as two specific projects, while the action still says “the projects the owner picks”
open_points.question: Is the one allowed production import restricted to the two named project ids, or may the owner choose a different subset when executing it?
options: Only the two recorded ids may be imported
Any subset of VPS projects may be selected once
The two ids are defaults that the owner may change before confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Treat the accepted two-id choice as fixed for the one production migration.

open_points.subject: customer relationship end date
open_points.text: The output is “marked as ended on that date,” but no text says whether the date is supplied by the owner or is the time Registry accepts the action
open_points.question: What date is recorded when ending a relationship, and may the owner record a historical effective date?
options: Registry always records its current date
The owner supplies the effective date
Registry defaults to today but accepts an explicit effective date
open_points.default_guess: Accept an owner-supplied effective date, defaulting to Registry's current date.

open_points.subject: personal data in retained artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-71 says an anonymised project “holds no personal value,” but R0-60 keeps its artifact pointers and R0-68 says a pointer value that breaks the writer rule “is not refused and does reach the agent”
open_points.question: How can anonymisation guarantee that retained pointer values do not identify a person when Registry never inspects them?
options: Require an owner attestation that retained pointers are non-identifying
Remove or redact pointer values during anonymisation
Permit anonymisation only when the project has no pointers
Treat the writer rule as sufficient despite unenforced violations
open_points.default_guess: Permit anonymisation only after an explicit owner attestation that retained pointer metadata is non-identifying; otherwise require whole deletion.

open_points.subject: audit event set
open_points.text: R0-58 records “changes to projects and customer records” but does not say whether this includes room creation, pointer publication or withdrawal, session registration, pending requests, request answers and active-project changes; it also says ordinary “agent calls” are not recorded
open_points.question: Which exact state-changing primary actions create audit entries?
options: Every accepted state-changing primary action
Only the event categories explicitly enumerated in R0-58
A separately enumerated subset including specified room, pointer and session events
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-58's enumerated categories as exhaustive until each additional event is explicitly named.

open_points.subject: Client Portal offline projection exception
open_points.text: The permitted copy is described only as holding “what the customer's own cabinet shows,” with the sole explicit exclusion “never a tax id”
open_points.question: Which exact Registry fields may Client Portal persist in its offline projection, particularly customer name, contact fields, project display name, address and object characteristics?
options: An explicit allowlist is defined here
Portal may persist every field its token can read except tax id
Portal may persist identity only
The projection is treated as an immutable issued publication with a separately defined payload
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit allowlist limited to project identity and the minimum publication fields, excluding customer contact and fiscal data.

open_points.subject: issued-document copy exception
open_points.text: “A document a service issues ... fixes the values of its date,” but “issued” and the point at which values become fixed are not defined
open_points.question: Which document states qualify for the persistence exception, and what happens to drafts, previews, regenerated documents and withdrawn publications?
options: Only finalized and externally issued immutable documents qualify
Every rendered document or draft qualifies
Each owning service defines its own qualifying terminal states in its contract
open_points.default_guess: Limit the exception to an immutable finalized document or publication with a recorded issue time; drafts and previews remain ordinary removable copies.
